notes: NF and SN values are paper/reference values used only for comparison.
Dashboard values must be calculated independently and must not be forced toward these values.
v5 recomputed every number under the operating-point-weighted PEM on the 6-channel logged state. These values are NOT interchangeable with the v4.1 table.
The SN column changed measurement condition: v4.1 SN was tension-only 0.3% at LPF 100 Hz; v5 SN is dual-channel 0.3%/0.3% at LPF 50 Hz. The two tables are not comparable cell by cell.
The SN column is a fixed-cadence comparison at T_log = 20 ms. Each excitation's own optimum falls at a different logging period, so this ranking is condition-dependent, not absolute.

At the fixed 20 ms cadence the tension family compresses into a 42.6-46.7% cluster in which ET1 is NOT uniquely worst. Compared at each excitation's own optimum, the multichannel toggle leads ET1 by nearly 19 pp.
ET3M is a single joint three-condition fit through the multi-condition cost, not an average of three separate per-operating-point fits.

NF.aggregation: 10-plant pooled median at a single seed

SN.aggregation: pooled median over 10 plants x 3 seeds

spread.note: v4.1 reported 1.3 pp; the v5 noise-free spread across all six types is 2.69 pp, with the multichannel types within 0.29 pp of one another and EV1 distinctly the lowest.

own_optimum_notes: EV1 attains the lowest error under noise by a wide margin (26.7% against a 42.6-46.7% tension-family cluster).
Under dual-channel noise ET1's optimum sits at 20 ms while the other excitations settle between 5 and 10 ms.
ET6's apparent 5 ms optimum is fragile to the noise realization.
The extra operating points of ET3M do not by themselves improve identification accuracy in this three-span study; where they help, the gain is confined to slow-transport plants.

conditioning_ranking.note: kappa(F) is on the weighted-residual scale F = sum_k J_k^T W^2 J_k, so only the ordering is interpretable. Accuracy is the fraction of runs with error < 5% over 10 plants and the five logging periods Tlog <= 20 ms (n = 50 per excitation, single seed).
